question: I'm a BA junior (P-025) with dual concentrations (Finance + BAT) and an Economics minor. I want to register for 60 units in Spring 2026 to accelerate graduation. What approvals do I need?

domain_contributions.policies: Normal load = ~360 units ÷ 8 semesters = 45 units. 60 units is an overload of 15 units. Overload up to 12 units above normal requires advisor approval; more than 12 extra units requires advisor to adjust S3 max units.
domain_contributions.courses: 60 units = approximately 5 × 12-unit courses or equivalent combination
domain_contributions.programs: P-025's graduation target and dual concentration workload make an overload tempting but risky; AW does not apply (P-025 is in good standing)

key_facts: 60 units = ~15 units above the ~45-unit normal load
Policy: advisor approval required for any overload; additional S3 adjustment required for overloads exceeding 12 units above normal
P-025 is in good standing — not blocked by AW
P-025 should discuss the overload with their academic advisor and explain the dual concentration rationale
Advisors cannot update max units in S3 until the Saturday after Registration Week
wrong_if_single_domain: Knowing only the overload policy cannot determine whether 60 units is a realistic load for P-025 without knowing their current unit accumulation and remaining requirements. Knowing only program requirements cannot determine the approval process.
common_mistake: Assuming good academic standing means overloads are automatically approved; not knowing the advisor approval + S3 adjustment process for large overloads
reasoning_chain: Step 1 (programs): P-025 has dual concentration + minor, justifying heavy load
Step 2 (courses): 60 units = ~5 courses, 15 units above normal load
Step 3 (policies): Overload >12 units above normal → advisor approval + S3 max adjustment required
Conclusion: P-025 needs explicit advisor approval and S3 adjustment; overload is not automatic even in good standing
